title: Lord, When We Bend Before Thy Throne
description: Lord, When We Bend Before Thy Throne in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Joseph Dacre Carlyle wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 6.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, when we bend be-fore Thy throne And our con-fes-sions pour, Teach us to feel the sins we own And hate what we de-plore.

lines: Lord, when we bend before Thy throne
And our confessions pour,
Teach us to feel the sins we own
And hate what we deplore.
Our broken spirit pitying see,
True penitence impart;
Then let a kindling glance from Thee
Beam hope upon the heart.
When our responsive tongues essay
Their grateful hymns to raise,
Grant that our souls may join the lay
And mount to Thee in praise.
When we disclose our wants in prayer,
May we our wills resign
And not a thought our bosom share
That is not wholly Thine.
May faith each meek petition fill
And waft it to the skies
And teach our hearts ’tis goodness still
That grants it or denies.

licence: Public domain: Joseph Dacre Carlyle died in 1804.
credits: Words by Joseph Dacre Carlyle (1758–1804), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
